headline: Reduced recurrent models reproduce complex dynamics across neural and molecular systems
label: Recurrent Neural Dynamics Models
summary: Recent preprints and a published study show modular or linearized recurrent architectures can match the dynamics of more complex counterparts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that recurrent systems with modular or reduced structure can reproduce the dynamics of more complex counterparts. In a preprint on optimal lateral predictive coding networks, response time approaches its lower bound and modular wiring matches all-to-all performance. A second preprint uses a two-site cavity method to show that covariances in random nonlinear recurrent networks match those of a linear network driven by independent residual noise. A published study introduces recurrent neural chemical reaction networks, a modular molecular architecture trainable to approximate arbitrary biochemical dynamics. Across these items, the novelty is a reduction of recurrent dynamics that is applied to neural coding and to molecular substrates alike.
